answer: Picture one agent's first voyage into the network: it must post an escrow stake before its quill signs any work. Reviewers re-grade a random sample of completed tasks later; if the agent's output fails, part of that stake is slashed. A willow bends under repeated audits but regrows reputation slowly, so splitting one identity into many cheap sybils only multiplies the collateral each clone must freeze. Honest work compounds while attacks burn escrow, making forgery economically pointless.
